item.title: Julian Sayin continues working with Ohio State QB Luke Fahey
item.description: Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin has remained with the team since suffering an injury against Indiana on Oct. 17. "It says a lot about Julian that he's not just off getting his rehab wherever," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "He's with the team and with Luke [Fahey] helping him out." Sayin was ruled out indefinitely following the 19-15 win over the Hoosiers , in which defensive lineman Mario Landino came down on Sayin's right arm during a sack in the fourth quarter. Sayin, a second-year starter, returned to Ohio State's sideline that day in a sling, which he was no longer wearing when the Buckeyes lost 41-28 to Oregon on Nov. 7. Before the injury, Sayin was on track to improve in most areas from his first season, throwing for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions, though his completion rate was down from 77% to 68.2%. He'd also shown more ability as a runner, scoring two rushing touchdowns. The Carlsbad, California, native was considered a 2027 NFL Draft option going into the season, but there was always a chance he could return to Ohio State next year, having two more years of eligibility. More: Will Julian Sayin return to Ohio State next year? What we know Sayin, one of the seven Ohio State captains this season, walked out for the coin toss before both games he's missed and stayed on the sideline with an earpiece and a play script in his hand. Day indicated that his presence, from the practices to games, has been significant for freshman quarterback Luke Fahey as Fahey navigates his new starting role. "He's just another voice for him," Day said. "Somebody who's actually not just coached it, but actually done it, run the plays that we're working on. So, I think Luke feels like he's got somebody there that he can go to and get some counsel on." Fahey threw for over 250 yards in losses to USC and Oregon, but he has struggled to find a rhythm. Against the Ducks , Fahey recorded 89.7% of his 360 passing yards in the first and fourth quarters, going 11-for-17 and throwing his lone interception during the stretch in between. "When you're playing with a young quarterback, there are times you have to adapt," Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith said. "We have a lot of different ways to do that, to take stress off the quarterback in terms of how we communicate play calls and different packages." Fahey had better stats in his starting debut compared to Sayin's first game in the 2025 season-opener against Texas, as Fahey went 21-for-38 for 260 yards and a touchdown while Sayin went 13-for-20 for 126 yards and a touchdown. However, the current freshman has had a smaller margin for error, with the defense allowing an average of 35.5 points over the last two games. item.description: Patrick Mahomes is on track to start Sunday in Atlanta after practicing in full Wednesday, just days after a hit to his throwing elbow had Kansas City holding its breath. The Chiefs listed their quarterback with no limitations, a sign the MRI results are holding up and the elbow strain is manageable. For a 6-2 team facing the 3-6 Falcons with a new receiver joining the offense, it was the best news the week could have opened with. Patrick Mahomes Returns to Practice Without Major Elbow Injury Scare The scare came late in the first half of Kansas City’s 35-12 win over the Jets. On second-and-10 from the Chiefs’ 37-yard line, Mahomes’ arm collided with Jets rookie David Bailey as he went to throw, and the strip-sack left him on the ground clutching his right elbow. He was checked out, then finished the game with 23 completions on 31 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns. The scan showed no major structural damage, only a strain that the medical staff will monitor for swelling and discomfort. Andy Reid called his quarterback day-to-day on Monday, and the head coach said the staff would track his recovery milestones through the week. The MRI results had already ruled out the worst-case outcomes. “Chiefs listed QB Patrick Mahomes as a full participant in today’s practice, putting him on track to play Sunday at Atlanta,” Adam Schefter wrote . Mahomes said the elbow has improved since Sunday and that he has been getting treatment at the team facility and at home. Final game designations will not come until later in the week. The Chiefs have been through a longer rehab than this one. item.title: Cowboys’ Dak Prescott refuses to make 49ers game about personal revenge
item.description: Dak Prescott has another opportunity to beat the San Francisco 49ers, but the Dallas Cowboys quarterback insists revenge is not driving him. The Cowboys host San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 15, with Prescott looking to help Dallas secure consecutive victories for the first time this NFL season. Prescott has experienced two painful playoff defeats against the 49ers. San Francisco eliminated Dallas in the 2021 and 2022 postseason, leaving the quarterback with unfinished business against the franchise. MORE: Jerry Jones defends Cowboys’ coaching budget with surprising oil business comparison However, Prescott does not want those results to define Sunday’s matchup. “ I want to beat them absolutely , and I’m not naive to what’s happened or my history against them,” Prescott told reporters. “But to put that on the rest of these guys or put that on the locker room, I think that’s stupid.” Dak Prescott wants momentum, not personal revenge Nov 8, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) reacts after a play during the second quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Cowboys enter Week 10 with a 4-5 record after beating the Indianapolis Colts 27-23. They now face a 49ers team sitting at 7-1. Prescott said the matchup offers Dallas an important opportunity to build momentum. “This is about us going in and getting a win and us trying to win this game and get some momentum going,” he said. He also stressed the importance of finally putting two victories together. “Get back-to-back wins for the first time this season and build off of that,” Prescott added. The quarterback has delivered strong numbers through nine games. He has completed 218 of 336 passes for 2,381 yards, 16 touchdowns and five interceptions. His recent form offers further encouragement. Prescott has thrown six touchdowns without an interception across his last three starts. However, Dallas must address its defensive problems against a strong San Francisco offense. The Cowboys have allowed 26.2 points per game this season. Prescott understands the challenge but wants his teammates focused on the opportunity. “What a great opportunity to do it against a 7-1 team,” he said. “It just so happens that it’d be the Niners. “So yeah, obviously I want to get a win and everybody and anybody in this building does for sure a bunch of different reasons. But at the end of the day, it’s a 7-1 team coming in here and we’ve got an opportunity to beat them.” MORE: NFL analyst tears into Dak Prescott’s contract after Cowboys’ collapse Beating San Francisco would mean more than ending a difficult run against one opponent for Dallas. item.title: Yankees pitching coach says quiet part out loud about Cam Schlittler’s Cy Young season
item.description: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Yankees pitching coach says quiet part out loud about Cam Schlittler’s Cy Young season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New York Yankees pitching coach Matt Blake praised Cam Schlittler following the right-hander’s unanimous American League Cy Young Award win. Schlittler received the honor Wednesday after his first full major league season. The 25-year-old finished with an AL-leading 1.95 ERA and struck out 239 batters across 33 starts. Speaking on MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM in a clip shared Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, Blake explained how Schlittler’s 2026 campaign exemplified the aggressive approach he wants the Yankees’ pitching staff to embrace. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “And you know, the big message for our whole group: just you know, you’re not going to have as much margin for on the edges. Obviously, our catchers do a great job back there, but you know we’ve got to be more aggressive in the strike zone on the whole. And he’s built to do that. You know he can live in the strike zone with his stuff.” The 25-year old Cam Schlittler is a unanimous Cy Young Award winner. #Yankees | 🔗 https://t.co/iXax8hxC8m pic.twitter.com/YcG0f5Mo1H — MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM (@MLBNetworkRadio) November 12, 2026 He averaged nearly five strikeouts per walk, pairing swing-and-miss ability with limited free passes throughout his first full MLB campaign. Schlittler went 14-6, issuing 49 walks over 193 2/3 innings. His combination of strikeouts and control accompanied one of the lowest qualifying ERAs in Yankees history. Only Spud Chandler’s 1.64 ERA in 1943 and Ron Guidry’s 1.74 in 1978 rank lower among the franchise’s qualifying starters. Schlittler received all 30 first-place votes for 210 points. Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease finished second, followed by Cleveland Guardians left-hander Parker Messick. The Massachusetts native became the Yankees’ seventh Cy Young winner, joining Guidry and Gerrit Cole as the franchise’s unanimous recipients. New York selected Schlittler in the seventh round of the 2022 draft out of Northeastern. Four years later, he holds the American League’s top pitching honor. Schlittler’s unanimous selection capped a breakout season that established him among MLB’s premier pitchers. item.title: Mack Brown names only team he sees winning national title, makes bold comparison
item.description: Earlier in Tuesday night’s live College Football Playoff rankings stream on The Triple Option, Urban Meyer called the Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide interchangeable, the two most talented teams in the country and a step above everyone else when both play their best. Rob Stone saved the final question for the show’s guest, Mack Brown, and asked which teams have the ability to win it all. Brown, who won a national title at the Texas Longhorns, named one. “I think Georgia is the best team in the country, period. And right now, I’m not sure I would say anybody else, Rob, because we’ve got three more weeks that things have to happen. And Georgia’s got Missouri, who’s beaten down a little bit now, at home. They’re at South Carolina, which they’ll have to play with that quarterback, and they got Georgia Tech. So Georgia should win and be in the championship game. Who do they play? That is Alabama … They can run the ball. The quarterback’s making good decisions. The one they lost, they made some poor decisions in that game against Auburn. But to me, they’re more like Indiana last year than anybody else I see. They’re running the ball. They’re stopping the run. They’re not making many decisions, and they’ve got a good kicking game,” Brown said . Sep 7, 2024; Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels head coach Mack Brown with the referee in the third quarter at Kenan Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Georgia is 8-1 and No. 1 in the committee’s rankings, and it has already beaten the team Brown expects it to see again in December, winning 20-17 in Tuscaloosa on Oct. 10. The comparison he reached for at the end is the bolder part of the answer. The Indiana Hoosiers went 16-0 last season, won the program’s first national title and did it with a team built on the line of scrimmage, averaging 40 rushing attempts per game while allowing 77.62 rushing yards per game entering the playoff, third-fewest in the country. The Auburn game is where Georgia broke Mack Brown’s formula The Bulldogs ran for 295 yards at the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday and held a top-10 opponent to 66 on the ground in a 42-7 win that snapped Ole Miss’ 16-game home winning streak. That is Brown’s first two requirements, running the ball and stopping the run, met against the best opponent on Georgia’s November schedule. The Auburn Tigers outrushed Georgia 192-113 in Athens on Oct. 17, with quarterback Byrum Brown carrying 26 times for 115 yards. Gunner Stockton threw two interceptions, matching his total from the first six games, then lost a fumble at the Auburn 46 with 58 seconds left and the score tied at 24. Auburn kicked the winning field goal as time expired, and Georgia’s Peyton Woodring had a 54-yard attempt blocked before halftime. Every item on Brown’s list went against Georgia that afternoon. item.title: UFC 334: Ciryl Gane vs Josh Hokit, main card predictions
item.description: The UFC returns to New York City, making its annual November trip to Madison Square Garden. As the UFC always does, the MSG card is stacked from top to bottom with big names and high-stakes matchups. Two title fights headline UFC 334, with the heavyweight championship between Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit at the top of the bill. Gane won the interim title at UFC Freedom 250, beating Alex Pereira via second-round TKO. MORE: Merab Dvalishvili, Usman Nurmagomedov fight video leaked online after hotel incident Since then, Tom Aspinall has had to relinquish the heavyweight title due to ongoing eye complications. As a result, Gane was upgraded to undisputed champion. Hokit is one of the fastest-rising contenders ever. In January of 2026, he was the first fight on the UFC 324 card. Now less than 11 months later, he’s headlining a numbered event at Madison Square Garden. It helps that heavyweight is the thinnest division in the sport and has needed a jolt of energy for years now, but Hokit took advantage of that. In the co-main event, the greatest female fighter and one of the best fighters ever in general returns. Amanda Nunes is back and looks to regain the women’s bantamweight title against reigning champion Kayla Harrison. This fight isn’t about bad blood, but it has history. Nunes and Harrison trained together at American Top Team. Nunes left the gym to open her own space, and did so knowing that Harrison was trending towards becoming an opponent. Both title fights should be highly entertaining, along with the rest of the card. Here are predictions for the main card of UFC 334. Main event: Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit Jun 14, 2026; Washington, D.C., UNITED STATES; Ciryl Gane reacts after a win against Alex Pereira (not pictured) during UFC Freedom 250 at White House South Lawn. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) In his brief UFC career so far, Hokit has run through his opponents. He’s overwhelmed them with his athleticism and speed advantage. Against Gane, Hokit won’t have that overwhelming advantage. Gane is known for his speed and elite footwork. On the feet, this fight should be a mismatch. Hokit won’t be able to just back Gane up towards the cage and throw haymakers. Gane’s lateral movement is too good, and his jab is lightning-quick. Hokit is a great wrestler, but he isn’t much of a submission threat when on the ground. That said, unless Gane is hurt on the feet before hitting the mat, Hokit likely won’t be able to just control Gane for most of the round. Unless theres a quick finish in the first round where Hokit pulls Gane into a brawl, Gane should be able to keep the fight at his pace. item.title: Jessie Bates didn't sleep before being traded to Jacksonville Jaguars
item.description: New Jacksonville Jaguars safety Jessie Bates has put in some serious hours playing catch up. The team traded for Bates ahead of the NFL trade deadline , bringing in the veteran to bolster their secondary as they try to make a push towards the postseason. He has been in the Miller Electric Center late into the night and back at it early in the morning since the trade, trying to get up to speed in Anthony Campanile’s defense. “I don't know if he's left here since he's been here,” Campanile jokingly told reporters on Nov. 12. “He's part of the coaching staff, I think. I walk around; I see him everywhere.” James Gladstone: Jaguars aren’t ‘all-in’ after NFL trade deadline moves While he hasn’t really stayed the night, Bates has been in the building consistently since arriving in Jacksonville. “I’ve had about five hours of sleep the last couple of nights,” the veteran defensive back said. “Hanging out with [defensive backs coach Anthony Perkins] and getting caught up to speed on installs and everything. Once you learn coverages, conceptually, you can understand what they’re doing over here.” The Jaguars acquired defensive linemen Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux in addition to Bates at the deadline, a clear sign that the organization is serious about their potential this year. Bates, who’s in the last year of his deal, spent four years with the Atlanta Falcons and had some of the best years of his career there. He recorded 14 interceptions, including three pick-sixes, and 11 forced fumbles during his time with the Falcons. His skillset seems like a perfect match for Campanile’s defense which has consistently been one of the best in the league at takeaways. The move immediately addresses an area of the roster that was hampered by the season-ending injury to Eric Murray . “He's just made a lot of great plays in his career,” Campanile said of Bates. “He gives us a guy that can do that here.” Emotional goodbye in Atlanta, excitement for future highlights Jessie Bates’ week When the trade was reported on the morning of Nov. 9 , Bates hadn’t even been to sleep yet. He played in a game with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain on Oct. 8, and returned from the overseas trip to news of him being sent to Jacksonville. His time with the Falcons proved he was one of the best at his position, earning All-Pro and Pro Bowl nods while captaining the Dirty Birds. But even further, his time there put a spotlight on the type of person he is. item.title: UConn men's basketball forward Nik Khamenia out six to eight weeks with foot injury
item.description: UConn sophomore forward Nik Khamenia will be out at least 6-8 weeks with a foot injury, the team announced on Thursday. "Nik will have surgery in the coming days and is expected to make a full recovery," coach Dan Hurley said in a statement . "He will be reevaluated in 6-8 weeks." UConn vs Wagner takeaways: Instant analysis: UConn men’s basketball cruises past Wagner Khamenia suffered a left foot injury in the first half of Monday's 83-41 win over Wagner . Before his injury, Khamenia had his best start of the season, scoring 11 points on 4-of-5 shooting from the field and 3-of-3 shooting from beyond the arc. The California native came to Storrs in the transfer portal after playing his freshman season at Duke. He was the replacement to longtime forward Alex Karaban, who was drafted by the Sacramento Kings in June. In his first two starts, Khamenia averaged 10.5 points and four rebounds. The earliest Khamenia could return would be around Christmas with the latest being sometime in the first week of January. Freshmen Colben Landrew and Egor Amosov are slated to fill Khamenia's minutes at small forward until he returns. Landrew has been solid through three games, averaging 10 points and 4.7 rebounds per game off the bench. Amosov wasn't in Hurley's regular rotation, but will be thrust into more minutes with Khamenia's injury. "I feel confident in the players that we have," senior forward Jayden Ross said on Monday. "We know that Nik's gonna do whatever he can to get back on the court because he loves basketball, and that's just the type of person he is. But whatever the situation is, we will hold it down for him. I'm pretty sure everybody got in the game today, and we had a lot that played significant minutes. We're all super confident in the depth that we have this year. So, I'm sure with whatever the situation is, we'll be in a good spot." item.title: UEFA Nations League: Olise extends scoring streak for France despite Zidane's first defeat at San Siro
item.description: UEFA Nations League: Olise extends scoring streak for France despite Zidane's first defeat at San Siro Michael Olise failed to score or assist in his last three games for FC Bayern, but the superstar opened the scoring for France against Italy in UEFA Nations League action on Thursday. However, the hosts recovered from their early setback to record a thoroughly deserved 3-1 win over Les Bleus. The 24-year-old winger extended his scoring run with France to four games as he was in the right place to punish Gigi Donnarumma, whose poor form at club level continued with a big mistake on his return to San Siro. Roberto Mancini’s side leveled the score before the half-time break with a goal from Francesco Pio Esposito. The older brother of Inter's striker, Sebastiano, missed a penalty-kick at the hour mark, but Davide Frattesi’s strike and a successful penalty later on from “Pio” sealed a 3-1 win for Gli Azzurri. Olise’s Bayern teammate Dayot Upamecano played the entire game, while Wolfsburg's Saël Kumbedi made his debut by replacing his former Lyon teammate Malo Gusto. Both teams now have ten points in the group, but Italy are ahead with a better head-to-head record. Despite suffering their first defeat under Zinedine Zidane, France will only need a draw against Türkiye in the final matchday in Bordeaux. Türkiye lost all five matches so far as former Wolfsburg and Werder Bremen attacking midfielder Kevin de Bruyne inflicted their latest defeat against Belgium on Thursday. item.title: Ravens' Jesse Minter is hoping to reverse the misery vs. Chargers
item.description: Things have been a challenge for Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter this NFL season. item.title: Kane hails ‘incredible’ Wembley reception on historic England night
item.description: Kane hails ‘incredible’ Wembley reception on historic England night Harry Kane reflected on a “crazy few weeks” after celebrating his record-breaking England cap and Ballon d’Or win with the Wembley crowd. The England captain was honoured before kick-off against Croatia with a tifo and presentation marking his 126th appearance, while he also showed off his Ballon d’Or trophy to the supporters. “It was amazing,” Kane said. “A big thank you to everyone here at the FA who organised it, with the tifo, the presentations, thank you to Luka Modric and the Croatian organisation for their gift as well. “Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game. It was just a special moment. “It’s been a crazy few weeks, a lot happening. Of course it’s an important moment in the history of our national team, you have to enjoy these moments but once the game started it was just full focus on that. “These occasions feel much better when you win and now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself.” Kane also spoke of the significance of sharing his Ballon d’Or success with England supporters. “To be able to share the Ballon d’Or with our fans is important because we haven’t won it for a long, long time,” he said. “Not just the 126 caps but also the Ballon d’Or was an important occasion to mark and to see the fans and the reception I got was incredible.” Kane marked the occasion by scoring the winner from the penalty spot in a 2-1 victory, and added that winning a major tournament with England remains his ultimate ambition. “I know if we win a major tournament, which is my ultimate goal and my biggest dream with England, then the celebrations around the whole country would be a special thing to witness. “I don’t think I need any more motivation to make that happen but it will be incredible if we can.” Reflecting on his recent achievements, Kane admitted they have not fully sunk in yet. “In the winter break when I’ve got a couple of weeks off and I’ll be on the beach somewhere, I’ll try and reflect on everything I’ve achieved, because these ones are probably the biggest in my career without a doubt.”

item.title: ‘They have an absolute right to do it’: President Trump calls for Cleveland to change name back to ‘Indians’
item.description: President Donald Trump gestures during his speech at a rally in support of Republican candidates in Ohio for the midterm election at The Covelli Centre in Youngstown, Ohio on October 12, 2026. President Donald Trump may be big on trying to rename some things, such as lakes and other bodies of water , but he’s still rankled about Cleveland’s Major League Baseball team changing its nickname. During an appearance on Hugh Hewitt’s Salem Radio talk show Thursday, Trump once again called for the Cleveland Guardians to go back to being the Indians. The franchise officially rebranded in 2021. Trump: “Anybody that changes the name of the Cleveland Indians to the Guardians does not deserve to be a governor or senator … I think they should change their name back to the Cleveland Indians and they have an absolutely right to do it. And I think that would be good.” https://t.co/p7pyzhyN49 — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 12, 2026 Trump takes aim at ‘Mr. Dolan’ The Guardians are owned by the Dolan family, with Paul Dolan serving as the CEO and controlling owner. At the beginning of the clip, Trump refers to a “Mr. Dolan” from the Cleveland organization as a “pretty impressive guy, good-looking guy” before a brief detour about New York Knicks owner Jim Dolan, Paul’s cousin and “a very good guy” as well. “Mr. Dolan ran for the Senate, he ran for a lot of things, and I was always able to take him out by one little phrase,” Trump said. “Anybody that changes the name of the Cleveland Indians to the Guardians does not deserve to be a governor or senator.” Now, the “Mr. Dolan” Trump is talking about is actually Paul’s brother Matt, who previously served as a member of the Ohio Senate and House of Representatives. He never ran for governor but did lose twice in Republican primaries for the 2022 and 2024 US Senate races in Ohio. Matt Dolan reportedly has a small ownership stake but is not involved in day-to-day operations of the Guardians. That hasn’t stopped Trump from criticizing him in the past and blaming the name change for the 61-year-old’s failed Senatorial runs. ‘They have an absolute right’ It’s worth noting that Guardians leadership has continuously said it has no plans to go back to the old moniker, instead opting to focus on the future of the current brand. That didn’t stop Trump from asking Hewitt, an Ohio native and Cleveland fan, if he wants the Indians back. Hewitt said he “doesn’t care” what they call the team if they can win a World Series, something Cleveland hasn’t done since 1948. He then brought up that he hopes Trump can intervene in the looming MLB lockout, but the Commander-in-Chief wasn’t finished with his original take. “I think they should change their name back to the Cleveland Indians and they have an absolute right to do it. And I think that would be good,” he told Hewitt. item.title: France ‘in disarray’ in first defeat of Zinédine Zidane era
item.description: France ‘in disarray’ in first defeat of Zinédine Zidane era Zinédine Zidane said that his side were “in disarray” in what was his first defeat as manager of the France national team. The defeat to Italy at the San Siro was Les Bleus’ first on Italian soil since 1962. France, who won three of their first four games during the first international break of the Zidane era, looked set to continue their strong start under their new manager. Profiting from a Gianluigi Donnarumma error, they took the lead through Michael Olise, who is emerging as the key player in this side. However, things fell apart. Sebastiano Esposito levelled up midway through the second half before Davide Frattesi gave Roberto Mancini’s side the lead just after the hour mark. Thereafter, Les Bleus were overrun and Esposito would complete the scoring in a 3-1 win in which the Italians also missed a penalty. Post-match, Zidane analysed the defeat in an interview with TF1: “When we were struggling, we didn’t manage to react within the framework of the game plan that we put in place. We did it at 0-0 or at 1-0, but as soon as they took the lead, we were in disarray, notably defensively. We won’t be worried. It is a part of football. item.title: Harry Kane marks historic 126th England cap with a little reminder of his greatness
item.description: Harry Kane was asked this week to name the lowest moment of his 125 England caps, and his mind travelled back to that evening in Qatar when he sent a penalty over Hugo Lloris’s crossbar and up to the heavens. Kane being Kane, he would score the next 30 penalties of his career. “It made me improve,” he said. “A lot of the bad things have helped me get to where I am now.” Perhaps it was apt, then, that on the night of his record-breaking 126th England cap, Kane scored his 92nd England goal from the penalty spot to settle this 2-1 win over Croatia and book a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals. It was a little display of his work ethic, a simple kick of the ball honed to a fine point through thousands of repetitions on the training ground. Kane dinked his penalty down the middle and a diving Dominik Livakovic almost blocked the ball with his trail leg. The goalkeeper beat the ground in frustration as if to say, I knew you’d do that. But perhaps this is the point: since that World Cup miss against France, Kane has trained every penalty into his armoury – the stutter or the run, the blast or the dink, left or right or the space a goalkeeper leaves behind – and Livakovic couldn’t cover them all. It came after a rare miss for Bayern Munich last month. “The next one is always important to bounce back,” Kane said. “I did my usual routine yesterday in training and looked at the goalkeeper. I haven’t gone down the middle with a penalty for maybe three or four years. With penalties, you have to keep things fresh, keep things moving. I thought it was a good time to do it, looking at his clips. Thankfully, it paid off today.” Kane's penalty evades the leg of Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic (PA) What did we learn from this slightly underwhelming performance? England are better than Croatia, but then we saw that at the World Cup when England beat them 4-2, and more emphatically in Rijeka last month when England won 7-0. This was naturally a more cautious Croatia, against an altogether sloppier England who made a series of uncharacteristic errors all over the field. Trent Alexander-Arnold gave the ball away on the edge of his own box, Lewis Hall played a fancy flick straight off the pitch and Jarell Quansah assisted Croatia’s equaliser with a deft, daft header inside his own six-yard box. Jude Bellingham showed frustration towards some of his teammates’ errors, yet his best game largely deserted him too. The England fans who shivered through these 90 minutes might instead remember the few moments beforehand. The commemorations began with a giant Tifo behind one goal displaying England’s captain roaring into the night sky with the words “England’s finest” and “Kane 126” emblazoned top and bottom. Kane emerged from the tunnel with his four children as mascots, and then spent a couple of minutes waving around the Ballon d’Or before being presented with three gifts, like a scene from the nativity. item.title: Delbarton soccer gets revenge against Seton Hall Prep, moves to final
item.description: MORRIS TOWNSHIP — Dylan Mazzarella called it "a full-circle moment," standing on Delbarton's soccer field and celebrating after defeating Seton Hall Prep, 3-2, in the NJSIAA Non-Public A North final. The Green Wave senior reflected back on four years ago, when the roles were reversed. This is Delbarton's first sectional title since 2018 – also defeating the Pirates, but on penalty kicks. Seton Hall Prep (14-7) had topped the Green Wave in the 2021 and 2023 finals, though the Green Wave has a 13-4-2 all-time lead in NJSIAA Tournament matches. "Freshman year, it was sad to go out on this field to Seton Hall, so it was great to beat them," said Mazzarella, a Parsippany resident. "We took advantage early, and they started getting back into the game. Knowing how we prepared, it got us through." Sophomore Cortland Martin figured into all three Green Wave goals, scoring the first two and taking the free kick that classmate Thine Sohn nodded in. A sophomore defender, Sohn had cleared a ball off the line with about two minutes to go before halftime, then scored the eventual game winner less than five minutes into the second half. Martin has five goals in Delbarton's three playoff games, and is the leading scorer with 23. More: Delbarton soccer coach's 'first recruit?' Newton coach's son "You can't really prepare for games like these," Sohn said. "But these are the games we play for. It means the world to me. At the end of the day, the job's not finished. We've got to keep our heads." Top-seeded Delbarton (21-1-1) already beat national powerhouse St. Benedict's Prep for the first time in three years, but Mazzarella noted the postseason is "a lot of games in not a lot of time." The lack of rest may have shown up as Seton Hall Prep scored twice in little more than three minutes late in the second half. The Green Wave has another quick turnaround to play South champion Pingry in the Non-Public A final at 3 p.m. Sunday at Franklin High School. The Big Blue defeated St. Augustine, 5-2, at the same time as the Green Wave's match. The Green Wave ranks third all-time with 13 NJSIAA titles, but hasn't won it all since 2017. Delbarton athletic director Tony Negrin handed the sectional trophy to junior midfielder Evan Johnson – a defensive stalwart against St. Benedict's – and he dashed over to the far side of the field, where his teammates were celebrating with hundreds of fans. "Nobody on this team knows what this is like, until now," longtime Delbarton coach David Donovan said. "It becomes a culture. It's extra special because they are reclaiming it for the alumni." item.title: Dan Patrick will delay retirement if his show wins Sports Emmy
item.description: Credit: The Dan Patrick Show Dan Patrick’s epically long retirement tour could be even longer if his radio show manages to win a Sports Emmy. It’s been more than three years since Patrick announced he would retire at the end of his current contract, saying he plans to step away from his radio show shortly after Super Bowl LXII, which will be played Feb. 13, 2028. Patrick gave himself and his fans four years to cope with the looming retirement . But Thursday morning, he admitted there’s a path to moving the goalposts, with one caller asking whether winning a Sports Emmy could change his mind. “If we win the Sports Emmy, I’ll stay another year.” https://t.co/hVEEb0TT7W — Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) November 12, 2026 “If we win the Sports Emmy, I’ll stay another year,” Patrick admitted. Producer Paul Pabst sought to clarify whether Patrick would stay one year from the time of winning an Emmy, or if he would add a full year to his contract with a win. “I would add another year to my contract,” Patrick admitted. Which means if The Dan Patrick Show wins a Sports Emmy next spring, the sports media legend will delay his 2028 retirement date by another 12 months. But Patrick was comfortable making the declaration because he’s confident it won’t happen. “We’re not gonna win the Sports Emmy, we’re not. I’m calling it. We’re not winning it,” Patrick insisted. “I just want us to get nominated. We’re going against these huge networks here! And there’s no reason why we shouldn’t be nominated with them. I just think that they can do some fancier things than we can.” Patrick won a Sports Emmy for “Outstanding Sports Personality – Studio Host” while at ESPN in 1997. But The Dan Patrick Show has not won or even been nominated, despite producing Emmy-worthy content, according to Patrick. It would certainly go against the grain for a sports radio show to receive an Emmy for “Outstanding Sports Studio Show – Daily” when going up against more TV-centric programs like First Things First or NFL Live . But none of those other shows are putting retirement on the line. If the Emmys want more Dan Patrick, they should figure out a way for his radio show to win an award. item.title: Dodgers Shopping Teoscar Hernandez Ahead of Offseason Frenzy
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernandez is firmly on the trade block , according to an insider, as the team’s offseason ramps up. According to MLB insider Bob Nightengale , Hernandez is on the trade block, and teams that miss out on some of the outfielders in free agency could target him. “They’ve got outfielder Teoscar Hernandez and his remaining $21 million salary on the trade block,” Nightengale wrote for USA Today. The Dodgers don’t need to deal Hernandez, since they can afford to keep his money on the books for one more year and still make other signings, namely, keep Tarik Skubal. He has just 10 stolen bases over the last two years, so speed isn’t a factor either. On a different team, where he can DH regularly and let his bat shine, Hernandez may still have another gear to offer, but with one more year to cash in on him in the trade market and a ton of players waiting on the wings, a deal makes more and more sense.
